This report provides an update on the 2022 quarter three financial forecasts.

Other positive items included in the forecast are 1.1 million dollars higher than anticipated municipal revenue sharing.
4.2 million surplus in transit from a faster recovery from the pandemic than originally anticipated and 2.2 million higher than anticipated investment income.

A $2.1 million shortfall in supplementary taxes due to some significant appeal losses becoming finalized.
$1.8 million deficit in recreation and culture due to a slower recovery in leisure centers than originally estimated.
$1 million shortfall in fines and penalties and 2.8 million shortfall in information technology from higher Microsoft licensing costs and cybersecurity investments.
As presented at the March 21st 2022 GPC meeting, the likelihood of a significant deficit in 2022 has been known for some time.
Several strategies were approved during that meeting which will need to be approved at year end.
